doc.title: Clark Terry interviewed by Joe Williams and Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, May 19, 1995

title: The African tour: playing with the Africans in Lagos
summary: Williams recalls the Lagos concert where the African orchestra borrowed Terry's white drummer David Adams; the ambassador sat in on trumpet.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Africa. I will never forget the trip to Africa with Clark Terry.
Oh, I shall always remember that too. It was marvelous.

One experience I must talk to you about, because to me it was thrilling and the dichotomy of it just killed me. The Africans decided in Lagos, after we did our concert, that they were going to entertain us with the African orchestra there.
Right. In Lagos. No it wasn’t the Greener. No they were just going to entertain us. They were going to play for us, the Africans.
And who was the kid that you had out of Westwood, on drums?

Adams, yeah. Here we were in Africa and I was in charge, and I went up to the microphone and asked if Mr. Adams would come up and please play with the Africans. Only in Africa. They couldn’t find their drummer.
This was a Caucasian drummer we had.
No, the drummer we had, David Adams, was a Caucasian drummer. He was the only Caucasian in the whole group. He had a drumset. This is funny.

Yeah, and the Africans were going to entertain us but they couldn’t find a drummer. So they wanted to know if they could borrow ours. So here we were in Africa and they were entertaining us, only they had a white drummer who was very, very happy. And the man there who was the ambassador I think he was to Lagos, right? And we did the television thing. He asked if he could sit in. Playing trumpet.
But the title of that was “He’s not our regular drummer.”
